records.source: הִנֵּ֥ה יֽוֹם־בָּ֖א לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְחֻלַּ֥ק שְׁלָלֵ֖ךְ בְּקִרְבֵּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Look, a day [is] coming for Yahweh, and will be divided your plunder in your midst.
pieces: Look, a day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming, when the plunder taken from you will be shared out within your walls.

L.1: Look, a day is coming for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when your plunder will be divided in your midst.

R.1: Listen, Jerusalem! A day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming. Your enemies will divide up the things they have taken from you, right inside your city.

decisions.choice: a day is coming for the LORD: the day of the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a day is coming that belongs to the LORD", as Isaiah 2:12 says that the LORD of hosts "has a day". It is the day the prophets call "the day of the LORD", when he comes to judge and to rescue (Joel 1:15, where the main note is; Amos 5:18-20). In this chapter it begins as a day of disaster for Jerusalem (verses 1-2) and becomes the day when the LORD fights for the city and is king over all the earth (verses 3-9).

decisions.choice: your plunder will be divided in your midst: Jerusalem's enemies share out her goods inside the city
decisions.reason: "Your" is feminine singular: the city of Jerusalem is spoken to as a woman, as often in the prophets. Victors divided the plunder after a battle (Judges 5:30; Isaiah 9:2). That they do it "in your midst" means that the city has fallen and the enemy is at ease inside it (verse 2). Verse 14 turns the picture round: the wealth of the nations is gathered in.

decisions.choice: a day of the LORD (B, R); within your walls (B); Listen, Jerusalem! ... Your enemies will divide up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "a day of the LORD", close to the wording set for "the day of the LORD" (Joel 1:15), while keeping the Hebrew "a day" (m1). Balanced says "within your walls" for "in your midst". Readable names Jerusalem, the city spoken to, and the enemies who divide the plunder (m2).

records.heading: A day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is coming

records.source: וְאָסַפְתִּ֨י אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֥ם׀אֶֽל־יְרוּשָׁלִַם֮ לַמִּלְחָמָה֒ וְנִלְכְּדָ֣ה הָעִ֗יר וְנָשַׁ֨סּוּ֙ הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים תִּשָּׁכַ֑בְנָה וְיָצָ֞א חֲצִ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֔ה וְיֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵ֖ת מִן־הָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem for battle, and will be captured the city, and will be plundered the houses, and the women will be lain with; and will go out half of the city into exile, and the rest of the people not will be cut off from the city.
pieces: I will gather all the nations to make war on Jerusalem. The city will be taken, its houses looted and its women raped. Half of the city will go off into exile, but those who remain will not be cut off from the city.

L.2: And I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle; and the city will be captured, and the houses plundered, and the women violated; and half of the city will go out into exile, but the remainder of the people will not be cut off from the city.

R.2: I will bring all the nations together to fight against Jerusalem. They will capture the city, rob the houses and rape the women. Half of the people of the city will be taken away as prisoners. But the others will not be taken from the city.

decisions.choice: I will gather all the nations: the LORD himself brings the attack on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks. The nations come because he gathers them, as in Joel 4:2 and Zephaniah 3:8, and as 12:2-3 has already said. The disaster of verses 1-2 is under his hand, and he turns it into judgment on the nations he has gathered (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the women will be violated: the written text has a blunter verb, which is read aloud as "be lain with"
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) give a coarse verb for rape, which is written the same way in Deuteronomy 28:30, Isaiah 13:16 and Jeremiah 3:2; in each place the reading tradition (qere) replaces it with "be lain with", a more modest word for the same act. The data gives the reading tradition. Both forms say that the women are raped.

decisions.choice: half the city into exile, the rest not cut off: a remnant stays
decisions.reason: Exile was the usual fate of the people of a captured city, as Jerusalem had known since 587 BC (2 Kings 25:11). Here only half go; the rest stay in the city. The prophets speak again and again of a remnant that comes through judgment (13:8-9; Isaiah 10:20-22).

decisions.choice: violated (L); raped (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the Hebrew means (m2), as the style guide asks for such passages; Literal keeps a word closer to the restraint of the reading tradition.

records.source: וְיָצָ֣א יְהוָ֔ה וְנִלְחַ֖ם בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם הָהֵ֑ם כְּי֥וֹם הִֽלָּחֲמ֖ובְּי֥וֹם קְרָֽב׃
records.gloss: And will go out Yahweh and will fight against those nations, as [the] day of his fighting on a day of battle.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will go out and fight against those nations, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fights on the day of battle.

L.3: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will go out and fight against those nations, as when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fights on a day of battle.

R.3: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will go out and fight against those nations. He will fight them as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} always fights on the day of battle.

decisions.choice: the LORD will go out and fight, as on a day of battle: the LORD as a warrior
decisions.reason: "The LORD will fight for you" was Moses' word at the sea (Exodus 14:14), and the song that followed calls the LORD "a warrior" (Exodus 15:3). Isaiah 42:13 says that the LORD "goes out like a warrior". The comparison is with the battles he has fought for his people before; the verse does not say which.

decisions.choice: those nations: the nations he gathered in verse 2
decisions.reason: The nations the LORD gathered against Jerusalem are the ones he now fights. He brought them to the city to judge them there, as Joel 4:2 and 4:12 say.

decisions.choice: as he always fights on the day of battle (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the comparison is with the LORD's way in battle, without naming a particular battle (m1). "He" and "his" for the LORD take the deity_pronoun setting.

records.source: וְעָמְד֣וּ רַגְלָ֣יו בַּיּוֹם־הַ֠הוּא עַל־הַ֨ר הַזֵּתִ֜יםאֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַם֮ מִקֶּדֶם֒ וְנִבְקַע֩ הַ֨ר הַזֵּיתִ֤ים מֵֽחֶצְיוֹ֙ מִזְרָ֣חָה וָיָ֔מָּה גֵּ֖יא גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וּמָ֨שׁ חֲצִ֥י הָהָ֛ר צָפ֖וֹנָה וְחֶצְיוֹ־נֶֽגְבָּה׃
records.gloss: And will stand his feet on that day on [the] Mount of the Olives, which [is] before [the] face of Jerusalem from [the] east; and will be split [the] Mount of the Olives from its middle eastward and westward, a valley great very; and will move half of the mountain northward and half of it southward.
pieces: On that day {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet will stand upon the Mount of Olives, which faces Jerusalem on the east. The Mount of Olives will split in two from east to west, opening a very wide valley, as half of the mountain moves north and the other half south.

L.4: And in that day {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which [is] facing Jerusalem to the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split from its middle, eastward and westward, [into] a very great valley; and half of the mountain will move northward, and half of it southward.

R.4: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The mountain will split in half from east to west, and a huge valley will open up. Half of the mountain will move toward the north, and half toward the south.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the ridge east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The ridge rises east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley, higher than the city. This is the only place in the Hebrew Bible where it is called "the Mount of Olives"; 2 Samuel 15:30 speaks of "the ascent of the olives", which David climbed weeping as he fled from Absalom. In Ezekiel's vision the glory of the LORD left the city and stood on "the mountain east of the city" (Ezekiel 11:23).

decisions.choice: his feet will stand: the LORD comes in person
decisions.reason: The LORD's feet standing on the mountain is a bold picture of his coming in person to fight for the city. The prophets picture the mountains shaking and splitting when he comes (Micah 1:3-4; Nahum 1:5; Habakkuk 3:6).

decisions.choice: the mountain split, a very great valley: a way of escape
decisions.reason: The split opens a valley through which the people flee (verse 5), as the sea was split for Israel to pass through; Exodus 14:16 and 14:21 use the same verb. In Acts 1:9-12 Jesus is taken up into heaven from the Mount of Olives, and the angels say that he will come back in the same way; many readers connect that promise with this verse.

decisions.choice: his feet will stand (L, B); the LORD will stand (R)
decisions.reason: "His" is the LORD, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting. Readable names the LORD and says that he will stand, since a new scene begins and "his feet" would leave the reader asking whose.

records.source: וְנַסְתֶּ֣ם גֵּֽיא־הָרַ֗י כִּֽי־יַגִּ֣יעַ גֵּי־הָרִים֮ אֶל־אָצַל֒ וְנַסְתֶּ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר נַסְתֶּם֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָרַ֔עַשׁ בִּימֵ֖י עֻזִּיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה וּבָא֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔י כָּל־קְדֹשִׁ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And you will flee [by the] valley of my mountains, for will reach [the] valley of [the] mountains to Azal; and you will flee as you fled from before the earthquake in [the] days of Uzziah king of Judah; and will come Yahweh my God, all [the] holy ones with you.
pieces: You will flee through the valley of my mountains, for the valley between the mountains will reach as far as Azal. You will run as you ran from the earthquake during the reign of Uzziah king of Judah. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God will come; all the holy ones will be with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.5: And you will flee [through] the valley of my mountains, for the valley of the mountains will reach to Azal; and you will flee just as you fled from the face of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah; and then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God will come, all the holy ones with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.5: You will escape through the valley of my mountains, because that valley will reach as far as Azal. You will run away, just as your ancestors ran from the earthquake while Uzziah was king of Judah. After that, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God will come, and all the holy ones will be with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: the earthquake of Amos 1:1
decisions.reason: Amos 1:1 dates Amos's words "two years before the earthquake", in the reign of Uzziah, in the middle of the eighth century BC. It was still remembered more than two hundred years later, and so was the flight from it. The coming flight will be like that one.

decisions.choice: you will flee: the Hebrew text, against the reading "will be blocked"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "you will flee" three times. The Septuagint, with the Targum, read the same consonants with other vowels as "will be blocked": "the valley of my mountains will be blocked ... as it was blocked by the earthquake". The record follows the Hebrew, which fits the new valley of verse 4 as a way of escape.

decisions.choice: Azal: a place not otherwise known
decisions.reason: No place called Azal is known for certain. It may be Beth-ezel (Micah 1:11) or some place near Jerusalem, and some take the word as a common noun, "the side". The point is that the valley reaches far enough for the people to escape.

decisions.choice: the valley of my mountains: who says "my" is not clear
decisions.reason: The LORD calls the mountains of the land "my mountains" in Isaiah 14:25 and 49:11, and this may be the LORD speaking, as in verse 2. But the same verse goes on to say "the LORD my God", which is the prophet's voice. The text does not settle who says "my".

decisions.choice: all the holy ones with you: the Hebrew text, against "with him"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "with you", as if the prophet turns to speak to the LORD as he comes. The Septuagint and other ancient versions, and some Hebrew manuscripts, read "with him", which runs more smoothly. The holy ones are the heavenly beings who come with the LORD (Deuteronomy 33:2-3; Psalm 89:6, 8). 1 Thessalonians 3:13 speaks of the coming of the Lord Jesus "with all his holy ones", in words close to the Greek of this verse.

decisions.choice: my mountains (no setting); with you (deity_pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: "You" is the prophet speaking to the LORD (m5), so it takes the deity_pronoun setting. "My" in "my mountains" takes none, since a setting would decide who is speaking (m4). "My God" is the prophet's word and takes none.

decisions.choice: in the days of Uzziah (L); during the reign of Uzziah (B); while Uzziah was king (R); your ancestors (R)
decisions.reason: The date follows the wording of Amos 1:1 at each level (m1). Readable says "your ancestors", since those who fled the earthquake lived two centuries earlier.

records.source: וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה א֔וֹר יְקָר֖וֹת וְקִפָּאֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And it will be on that day [that] not will be light; splendid [ones] and frost.
pieces: On that day there will be no light; the shining lights will grow dim.

L.6: And it will be in that day [that] there will be no light; the splendid [lights] will congeal.

R.6: At that time there will be no light. The bright lights in the sky will fade.

decisions.choice: the splendid lights will congeal: a very uncertain text
decisions.reason: The last words are hard. The reading tradition (qere) has "splendid things and frost"; the written consonants (ketiv) can be read "the splendid ones will congeal", that is, the bright lights of the sky will thicken and grow dim. Job 31:26 uses the word "splendid" of the moon moving in its brightness. The Septuagint and other ancient versions read "there will be no light, and cold and frost". The record follows the written consonants, read as the lights growing dim.

decisions.choice: no light: the darkness of the day of the LORD
decisions.reason: The prophets say that the sun, moon and stars will be darkened on the day of the LORD (Isaiah 13:10; Joel 2:10; 3:4; 4:15; Amos 5:18-20; 8:9). Verse 7 goes on to say that on this day evening will bring light.

decisions.choice: will congeal (L); will grow dim (B); will fade (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the verb, which is used of water thickening (Exodus 15:8); Balanced and Readable say what it means for light (m1). Readable says "in the sky".

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה יוֹם־אֶחָ֗ד ה֛וּא יִוָּדַ֥ע לַֽיהוָ֖ה לֹא־י֣וֹם וְלֹא־לָ֑יְלָה וְהָיָ֥ה לְעֵֽת־עֶ֖רֶב יִֽהְיֶה־אֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And it will be one day — it is known to Yahweh — not day and not night; and it will be at [the] time of evening [that] there will be light.
pieces: It will be a day like no other, a day known to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, without day or night; and when evening comes, there will be light.

L.7: And it will be one day, which is known to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, not day and not night; and it will be at evening time [that] there will be light.

R.7: It will be a day unlike any other, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} knows that day. It will not be day and then night. When evening comes, there will still be light.

decisions.choice: one day: a single, unique day
decisions.reason: "One day" can mean a day that is one of a kind (compare Ezekiel 7:5, "a disaster, a unique disaster"). It recalls the first day of creation, which Genesis 1:5 calls "one day": there God divided light from darkness and day from night; here there is no such division. Some take "one day" as one unbroken day.

decisions.choice: it is known to the LORD: the LORD knows that day
decisions.reason: The words stand as an aside. They may mean that the LORD knows when the day will come, or that the day is the LORD's and its nature is known to him, beyond human reckoning. Compare Matthew 24:36, where Jesus says that no one knows that day or hour but the Father.

decisions.choice: not day and not night; at evening there will be light: a new order of time
decisions.reason: God set day and night in their order and promised that they would not cease while the earth lasts (Genesis 8:22; Jeremiah 33:20). On this day the order changes: evening does not bring darkness. Isaiah 60:19-20 promises that the LORD will be his people's everlasting light, and Revelation 21:25 and 22:5 say that there will be no night in the new Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a day like no other (B); a day unlike any other (R); without day or night (B); not day and then night (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "one day" means here (m1). Readable explains "not day and not night" as the end of the change from day to night, which the next words describe.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יֵצְא֤וּ מַֽיִם־חַיִּים֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם חֶצְיָ֗ם אֶל־הַיָּם֙ הַקַּדְמוֹנִ֔י וְחֶצְיָ֖ם אֶל־הַיָּ֣ם הָאַחֲר֑וֹן בַּקַּ֥יִץ וּבָחֹ֖רֶף יִֽהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be on that day [that] will go out living waters from Jerusalem, half of them to the eastern sea and half of them to the western sea; in summer and in winter it will be.
pieces: On that day living water will flow out of Jerusalem, half of it to the eastern sea and half of it to the western sea. It will flow in summer and in winter alike.

L.8: And it will be in that day [that] living waters will go forth from Jerusalem, half of them to the eastern sea and half of them to the western sea; in summer and in winter it will be [so].

R.8: At that time living water will flow out from Jerusalem. Half of it will flow east to the Dead Sea, and half of it west to the Mediterranean Sea. It will keep flowing all year round, in summer and in winter.

decisions.choice: living waters: fresh, flowing water that gives life
decisions.reason: "Living water" is running water from a spring or stream, not the still water of a cistern (Genesis 26:19; Leviticus 14:5). Jeremiah 2:13 calls the LORD "the spring of living water". The phrase also means water that gives life, as the river of Ezekiel 47 brings life wherever it goes.

decisions.choice: the eastern sea and the western sea: the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the front sea", the one in front of a person who faces east, and "the back sea". They are the Dead Sea to the east of Jerusalem and the Mediterranean to the west, as in Joel 2:20. In a dry land where most streams fail in summer (Jeremiah 15:18; Job 6:15-17), water that flows summer and winter is a great gift.

decisions.choice: water flowing from Jerusalem: Ezekiel 47, Joel 4:18 and Revelation 22:1
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 47:1-12 sees a river flowing out from the temple east to the Dead Sea and making its salt water fresh. Joel 4:18 sees a spring flowing out from the LORD's house. Revelation 22:1 shows the river of the water of life flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb in the new Jerusalem. On the last day of the Festival of Booths, the festival named in verses 16-19, Jesus spoke of rivers of living water (John 7:37-38). See also 13:1.

decisions.choice: living waters (L); living water (B, R); the Dead Sea, the Mediterranean Sea (R)
decisions.reason: "Living water" is kept at every level, so that the reader can follow the picture into John 7:38 and Revelation 22:1 (m3); Balanced and Readable use the singular, as English does for water. Readable names the two seas (m2) and says "all year round".

records.source: וְהָיָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִהְיֶ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶחָ֖ד וּשְׁמ֥וֹ אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And will be Yahweh king over all the earth; on that day will be Yahweh one, and his name one.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will be king over all the earth. On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be one, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name one.

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be king over all the earth; in that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be one, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name one.

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will be king over the whole earth. At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be one, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name will be one.

decisions.choice: the LORD will be one, and his name one: the words of Deuteronomy 6:4
decisions.reason: The words take up Israel's confession, "Hear, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4). What Israel confesses will then be true for the whole earth: the LORD alone will be worshiped as God, and his name alone will be called on, with no other gods named beside him (13:2; Zephaniah 3:9). As in Deuteronomy 6:4, "one" can mean both "one" and "the only one".

decisions.choice: the LORD will be king over all the earth
decisions.reason: The psalms praise the LORD as "a great king over all the earth" (Psalm 47:3, 8; 96:10; 97:1). On that day his rule will be seen by all. Verses 16-17 call him "the King, the LORD of hosts", to whom the nations come to bow down; the king who comes to Zion in 9:9 is spoken of in the same book.

decisions.choice: the LORD will be one, and his name one (L, B); and his name will be one (R)
decisions.reason: The words follow Deuteronomy 6:4 as published ("the LORD is one") at each level. Readable stays close to Balanced, adding only "will be", since any plainer wording would have to choose between "one" and "only", as the notes at Deuteronomy 6:4 also say (m1). "His" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

records.source: יִסּ֨וֹב כָּל־הָאָ֤רֶץ כָּעֲרָבָה֙ מִגֶּ֣בַע לְרִמּ֔וֹן נֶ֖גֶב יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְֽרָאֲמָה֩ וְיָשְׁבָ֨ה תַחְתֶּ֜יהָ לְמִשַּׁ֣עַר בִּנְיָמִ֗ן עַד־מְק֞וֹם שַׁ֤עַר הָֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ עַד־שַׁ֣עַר הַפִּנִּ֔ים וּמִגְדַּ֣ל חֲנַנְאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד יִקְבֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: Will be changed all the land like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem; and she will be high and will dwell in her place, from [the] Gate of Benjamin to [the] place of the First Gate, to [the] Gate of the Corners, and [the] Tower of Hananel to the winepresses of the king.
pieces: The whole land will become like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will stand high and remain on its own site, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the First Gate and on to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel as far as the royal winepresses.

L.10: All the land will be turned [into something] like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; but she will be raised high and will remain in her place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the place of the First Gate, to the Gate of the Corners, and [from] the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.

R.10: All the land from Geba in the north to Rimmon south of Jerusalem will become flat, like the Jordan Valley. But Jerusalem will be raised up high, and it will stay where it is. It will reach from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate and the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel down to the king's winepresses.

decisions.choice: like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon: the hill country of Judah made flat
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep, flat valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, running on south to the Gulf of Aqaba. Geba lay about six miles north of Jerusalem and marked the northern edge of Judah (2 Kings 23:8, "from Geba to Beersheba"). Rimmon is most likely En-rimmon in the far south (Joshua 15:32; Nehemiah 11:29). The hills of Judah between them will be levelled.

decisions.choice: she will be raised high and will remain in her place: Jerusalem lifted above the land
decisions.reason: "She" is Jerusalem. As the land around is levelled, the city stands high, like the mountain of the LORD's house raised above the hills in Isaiah 2:2 and Micah 4:1. To "remain in her place" is to be lived in again on her old site, as 12:6 says.

decisions.choice: the gates, the tower and the winepresses: the bounds of the city
decisions.reason: The places mark the city's full extent. The Gate of Benjamin was in the north wall (Jeremiah 37:13; 38:7). The Corner Gate was at the northwest corner (2 Kings 14:13; Jeremiah 31:38). The Tower of Hananel stood in the north wall (Jeremiah 31:38; Nehemiah 3:1). The king's winepresses were probably in the south, near the king's garden (Nehemiah 3:15). The First Gate is not named elsewhere, and its place is unknown. Jeremiah 31:38-40 also promises that the city will be rebuilt from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.

decisions.choice: like the Jordan Valley; in the north (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the Jordan Valley" for the Arabah, which most readers will not know, and "in the north" for Geba, to show that the two places mark the length of the land (m1). Balanced says "Jerusalem" for "she".

records.source: וְיָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ וְחֵ֖רֶם לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־ע֑וֹד וְיָשְׁבָ֥ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לָבֶֽטַח׃
records.gloss: And they will dwell in her, and destruction not will be again; and will dwell Jerusalem in security.
pieces: People will live in it, and it will never again be devoted to destruction. Jerusalem will live in safety.

L.11: And they will dwell in her, and there will no longer be a ban of destruction; and Jerusalem will dwell in security.

R.11: People will live in Jerusalem, and it will never again be doomed to destruction. The city will be safe.

decisions.choice: destruction: the ban, total destruction given over to God
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for things or peoples "devoted" to God for complete destruction, as Jericho was (Joshua 6:17-18), and for the curse with which Malachi 3:24 closes the prophets. Jerusalem itself had been given over to such judgment (Isaiah 43:28). Never again will that happen to the city. Revelation 22:3 says of the new Jerusalem that there will no longer be any curse.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem will dwell in security
decisions.reason: Living in safety is the covenant blessing of Leviticus 25:18-19 and 26:5, and it is promised again to restored Israel (Jeremiah 23:6; 33:16; Ezekiel 34:25-28).

decisions.choice: a ban of destruction (L); devoted to destruction (B); doomed to destruction (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the sense of something given over to God to be destroyed (m1); Readable says "doomed".

records.source: וְזֹ֣את׀תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה הַמַּגֵּפָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִגֹּ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר צָבְא֖וּ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם הָמֵ֣ק׀בְּשָׂר֗וֹ וְהוּא֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עַל־רַגְלָ֔יו וְעֵינָיו֙ תִּמַּ֣קְנָה בְחֹֽרֵיהֶ֔ן וּלְשׁוֹנ֖וֹ תִּמַּ֥ק בְּפִיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And this will be the plague with which will strike Yahweh all the peoples who have waged war against Jerusalem: making rot his flesh while he [is] standing on his feet, and his eyes will rot in their sockets, and his tongue will rot in their mouth.
pieces: This is the plague with which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike all the peoples who made war on Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are still on their feet; their eyes will rot in their sockets; their tongues will rot in their mouths.

L.12: And this will be the plague with which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike all the peoples who have waged war against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are standing on their feet, and their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongue will rot in their mouth.

R.12: This is the plague {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send on all the nations that fought against Jerusalem. Their flesh will rot while they are still standing up. Their eyes will rot in their sockets. Their tongues will rot in their mouths.

decisions.choice: the plague: a blow from the LORD
decisions.reason: The word for "plague" comes from the verb "strike", used just after it. It is used of the blows the LORD sent on Egypt (Exodus 9:14) and on Israel in the wilderness (Numbers 14:37; 17:13-15). The verse says what the plague does, and no more.

decisions.choice: his flesh ... their mouth: the Hebrew speaks of each one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves between the singular ("his flesh", "he is standing", "his eyes", "his tongue") and the plural ("their sockets", "their mouth"). It means that the plague strikes each one of the enemy. The first verb is causative, "making his flesh rot": the LORD is the cause. The flesh rots "while he is standing on his feet", before the body has fallen.

decisions.choice: the LORD strikes the peoples who attacked Jerusalem
decisions.reason: When the Assyrian army besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's day, the angel of the LORD struck it down in one night (2 Kings 19:35; Isaiah 37:36). Here the LORD strikes the peoples who have made war on the city.

decisions.choice: their flesh ... their tongue (L); their tongues ... their mouths (B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level says "their" for the Hebrew singular (m2), and Literal keeps the Hebrew "tongue" and "mouth" in the singular. No level adds to what the Hebrew says the plague does. "Rot" is kept three times, as the Hebrew repeats its verb.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא תִּֽהְיֶ֧ה מְהֽוּמַת־יְהוָ֛ה רַבָּ֖ה בָּהֶ֑ם וְהֶחֱזִ֗יקוּ אִ֚ישׁ יַ֣ד רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְעָלְתָ֥ה יָד֖וֹ עַל־יַ֥ד רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And it will be on that day [that] will be a panic of Yahweh great among them; and they will seize each [the] hand of his fellow, and will go up his hand against [the] hand of his fellow.
pieces: On that day a great panic from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will fall on them. They will seize one another by the hand, and each will raise a hand against the other.

L.13: And it will be in that day [that] a great panic from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be among them; and they will seize each the hand of his fellow, and his hand will rise against the hand of his fellow.

R.13: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will throw them into great panic. They will grab hold of one another and attack each other.

decisions.choice: a great panic from the LORD: the enemy turns on itself
decisions.reason: The LORD threw the enemies of his people into great confusion (Deuteronomy 7:23; 1 Samuel 14:20). In Gideon's battle and in Jehoshaphat's the enemy armies destroyed one another (Judges 7:22; 2 Chronicles 20:23), and Ezekiel 38:21 says the same of the army of Gog.

decisions.choice: seize the hand of his fellow, and raise his hand against his fellow's hand: they fight one another
decisions.reason: To seize someone's hand can be to grapple with him, and to raise one's hand against someone is to attack him (2 Samuel 18:28; 20:21). In the panic the soldiers in the camps (verse 15) grab and strike at one another.

decisions.choice: each ... his fellow (L); one another, the other (B); one another, each other (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "each ... his fellow", used here of the soldiers of the enemy armies (m2), so it takes no gender setting. Balanced and Readable say "one another". Readable says "throw them into great panic" for "a great panic from the LORD will be among them".

records.source: וְגַ֨ם־יְהוּדָ֔ה תִּלָּחֵ֖ם בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֻסַּף֩ חֵ֨יל כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֜ם סָבִ֗יב זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֛סֶף וּבְגָדִ֖ים לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And also Judah will fight at Jerusalem; and will be gathered [the] wealth of all the nations around, gold and silver and garments, in abundance very great.
pieces: Judah too will fight at Jerusalem. Riches from all the nations round about will be collected: gold, silver and clothing in great quantity.

L.14: And Judah too will fight at Jerusalem; and there will be gathered the wealth of all the nations round about, gold and silver and garments, in very great abundance.

R.14: The people of Judah will also fight at Jerusalem. The riches of all the nations around them will be gathered up: huge amounts of gold, silver and clothing.

decisions.choice: fight at Jerusalem: in the city's defense, or against it
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "at" or "in", and also "against". Most read the verse as Judah fighting at Jerusalem, beside the city against the nations, as in 12:5-8. In 12:2 Judah too is caught up in the siege of Jerusalem, and some read this verse as Judah fighting against Jerusalem, forced by the enemy. The record says "at", which leaves the question open.

decisions.choice: the wealth of the nations gathered: the plunder of verse 1 reversed
decisions.reason: In verse 1 the enemy divided Jerusalem's plunder inside the city; now the wealth of the nations is gathered in. Haggai 2:7-8 and Isaiah 60:5, 11 also promise that the wealth of the nations will come to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: The people of Judah; huge amounts of (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Judah" for "Judah", and "huge amounts" for "in very great abundance".

records.source: וְכֵ֨ן תִּֽהְיֶ֜ה מַגֵּפַ֣ת הַסּ֗וּס הַפֶּ֨רֶד֙ הַגָּמָ֣ל וְהַחֲמ֔וֹר וְכָ֨ל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּמַּחֲנ֣וֹת הָהֵ֑מָּה כַּמַּגֵּפָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And so will be [the] plague of the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey, and all the livestock that will be in those camps, like this plague.
pieces: A plague like this one will also strike the horses, mules, camels and donkeys, and all the animals that are in those camps.

L.15: And so will be the plague of the horse, the mule, the camel and the donkey, and all the livestock that will be in those camps, like this plague.

R.15: The same kind of plague will also strike the horses, mules, camels and donkeys, and all the other animals in the enemy camps.

decisions.choice: the horse, the mule, the camel and the donkey: the animals of an army's camp
decisions.reason: Armies used horses for chariots and riders, and mules, camels and donkeys to carry their supplies. The plague that strikes the enemy soldiers (verse 12) strikes their animals too, so that the whole army is struck. One of the plagues on Egypt struck "the horses, the donkeys, the camels" (Exodus 9:3).

decisions.choice: A plague like this one will also strike (B); The same kind of plague (R); the enemy camps (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring "like this plague" from the end of the verse to the start, and Readable says whose camps they are.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כָּל־הַנּוֹתָר֙ מִכָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַבָּאִ֖ים עַל־יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְעָל֞וּ מִדֵּ֧י שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֗ה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺת֙ לְמֶ֨לֶךְ֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְלָחֹ֖ג אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And it will be [that] every one who remains of all the nations that came against Jerusalem, they will go up as often as year by year to bow down to [the] King, Yahweh of hosts, and to celebrate the festival of booths.
pieces: Then all who survive from all the nations that attacked Jerusalem will go up every year to worship the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and to keep the Festival of Booths.

L.16: And it will be [that] every survivor of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year by year to bow down to the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, and to keep the festival of booths.

R.16: All the people who are left alive from the nations that attacked Jerusalem will go up there every year. They will come to worship the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and to celebrate the Festival of Booths.

decisions.choice: the survivors of the nations will go up to worship: the nations join in Israel's worship
decisions.reason: Those who came to fight against Jerusalem come back as worshipers. The prophets look for the nations to come to Zion to learn the LORD's ways and to worship him (Isaiah 2:2-3; 66:23; Micah 4:1-2; Zechariah 8:20-23). "Go up" is the word for the pilgrimage to Jerusalem, which stands high in the hills (Psalm 122:4).

decisions.choice: the festival of booths: the autumn festival at the end of the harvest
decisions.reason: The Festival of Booths was kept for seven days from the fifteenth day of the seventh month, in the autumn, when the harvest was gathered in (Leviticus 23:34-43; Deuteronomy 16:13-15). It was one of the three festivals at which every man in Israel was to appear before the LORD (Deuteronomy 16:16). Israel lived in huts of branches to remember the journey through the wilderness after the LORD brought them out of Egypt (Leviticus 23:42-43). Now the nations are called to keep it.

decisions.choice: the King, the LORD of hosts
decisions.reason: Isaiah saw "the King, the LORD of hosts" in the temple (Isaiah 6:5), and verse 9 has said that the LORD will be king over all the earth. The pilgrims come to bow before him as subjects before their king.

decisions.choice: bow down (L); worship (B, R); the festival of booths (L); the Festival of Booths (B, R); the King (every level)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 23:34, Literal writes "the festival of booths" and Balanced and Readable "the Festival of Booths". The verb means to bow down, the act of worship; Balanced and Readable say "worship". "The King, the LORD of hosts" follows the published wording of Isaiah 6:5, and "the LORD of hosts" the wording set in Isaiah.

records.source: וְ֠הָיָה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֜ה מֵאֵ֨ת מִשְׁפְּח֤וֹת הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֔ת לְמֶ֖לֶךְ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃
records.gloss: And it will be [that] whoever not will go up from the families of the earth to Jerusalem to bow down to [the] King, Yahweh of hosts, and not on them will be the rain.
pieces: If any of the families of the earth fail to go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, no rain will fall on them.

L.17: And it will be [that] whichever of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to bow down to the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, on them there will be no rain.

R.17: Any of the peoples of the world that do not travel up to Jerusalem to worship the King, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, will get no rain.

decisions.choice: the families of the earth: the words of the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: "All the families of the earth" will be blessed in Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:3; 28:14). Here the families of the earth are called to come to Jerusalem to worship.

decisions.choice: no rain: the gift the season needed
decisions.reason: The Festival of Booths came at the end of the dry summer, just before the autumn rains on which the next year's crops depended. The LORD gives or withholds the rain (Deuteronomy 11:13-17; 1 Kings 17:1; Amos 4:7). Those who refuse to honor him as King will not receive his gift.

decisions.choice: the peoples of the world (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "peoples" for "families", since the word means the clans and nations of the earth, not households.

records.source: וְאִם־מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת מִצְרַ֧יִם לֹֽא־תַעֲלֶ֛ה וְלֹ֥א בָאָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה הַמַּגֵּפָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִגֹּ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יַֽעֲל֔וּ לָחֹ֖ג אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And if [the] family of Egypt not will go up and not come, and not on them; will be the plague with which will strike Yahweh the nations that not will go up to celebrate the festival of booths.
pieces: If the people of Egypt do not go up and come, they will have no rain either; the plague will come on them with which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} strikes the nations that do not go up to keep the Festival of Booths.

L.18: And if the family of Egypt does not go up and does not come, then not on them [will the rain fall]; there will be the plague with which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} strikes the nations that do not go up to keep the festival of booths.

R.18: If the people of Egypt do not go up to Jerusalem, they too will get no rain. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will strike them with the plague {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends on the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.

decisions.choice: and not on them: a hard text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "and not on them", with no verb, so "the rain" of verse 17 must be understood: they too will have no rain. Egypt did not depend on rain but on the yearly flooding of the Nile (Deuteronomy 11:10-11), and this may be why the plague is named as Egypt's punishment. The Septuagint and the Syriac do not have "not", and read "then on them will come the plague". The record follows the Hebrew, supplying "rain" from verse 17.

decisions.choice: the family of Egypt: Egypt as one of the families of the earth
decisions.reason: Egypt, Israel's oppressor of old, is named as one of the "families of the earth" of verse 17, and so as one of the peoples called to worship in Jerusalem (compare Isaiah 19:19-25).

decisions.choice: [will the rain fall] (L); they will have no rain either (B); they too will get no rain (R)
decisions.reason: Every level supplies the rain from verse 17 (m1), and Literal brackets it. Readable leaves out "and come", which repeats "go up", and says "to Jerusalem".

records.source: זֹ֥את תִּהְיֶ֖ה חַטַּ֣את מִצְרָ֑יִם וְחַטַּאת֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יַֽעֲל֔וּ לָחֹ֖ג אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: This will be [the] sin of Egypt and [the] sin of all the nations that not will go up to celebrate the festival of booths.
pieces: This will be the punishment for Egypt, and the punishment for all the nations that do not go up to keep the Festival of Booths.

L.19: This will be Egypt's punishment, and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to keep the festival of booths.

R.19: This is how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will punish Egypt and all the other nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.

decisions.choice: punishment: the word for "sin", used for what sin brings
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for sin. Like the word for "iniquity" (Genesis 4:13; Lamentations 4:6), it can also mean the penalty that sin brings, and that is its sense here: this is what Egypt and the nations will suffer for refusing to come.

decisions.choice: punishment (every level); This is how the LORD will punish (R)
decisions.reason: Literal also says "punishment", since "the sin of Egypt" would not say what the word means here (m1). Readable names the LORD, who sends the plague (verse 18).

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ עַל־מְצִלּ֣וֹת הַסּ֔וּס קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֤ה הַסִּירוֹת֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה כַּמִּזְרָקִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: On that day will be on [the] bells of the horse, "Holiness to Yahweh"; and will be the pots in [the] house of Yahweh like the bowls before the altar.
pieces: On that day the bells of the horses will bear the words "Holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}", and in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the cooking pots will be like the bowls in front of the altar.

L.20: In that day there will be [written] on the bells of the horses, "Holiness to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}"; and the pots in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be like the bowls before the altar.

R.20: At that time even the bells on the horses will have the words "Holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}" written on them. The cooking pots in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be as holy as the bowls used at the altar.

decisions.choice: Holy to the LORD: the words on the high priest's gold plate
decisions.reason: "Holy to the LORD" was engraved on the gold plate on the high priest's turban (Exodus 28:36; 39:30). It marked him as set apart to the LORD. On that day the same words will be on the bells of horses, once the animals of war (9:10). What was written for the high priest alone will be true of ordinary things.

decisions.choice: bells: small bells or metal discs on a horse's harness
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It is related to the word for cymbals and to a verb meaning "to ring", and it means bells or metal plates hung on a horse's harness.

decisions.choice: the pots ... like the bowls before the altar
decisions.reason: The pots were for cooking the meat of the sacrifices that worshipers ate (1 Samuel 2:13-14). The bowls were the basins used at the altar to catch the blood of the sacrifices and splash it on the altar (Exodus 27:3; 38:3; Numbers 7:13). The plainest vessels in the temple will be as holy as the most sacred.

decisions.choice: "Holiness to the LORD" (L); "Holy to the LORD" (B, R); as holy as (R)
decisions.reason: The inscription follows Exodus 28:36 at each level: Literal keeps the noun "Holiness", and Balanced and Readable say "Holy". Literal brackets "written", Balanced says "bear the words", and Readable explains the comparison of pots and bowls (m3). Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD".

records.source: וְ֠הָיָה כָּל־סִ֨יר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם וּבִֽיהוּדָ֗ה קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבָ֨אוּ֙ כָּל־הַזֹּ֣בְחִ֔ים וְלָקְח֥וּ מֵהֶ֖ם וּבִשְּׁל֣וּ בָהֶ֑ם וְלֹא־יִהְיֶ֨ה כְנַעֲנִ֥י ע֛וֹד בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And will be every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah holy to Yahweh of hosts, and will come all those who sacrifice and will take from them and will boil in them; and not will be a trader again in [the] house of Yahweh of hosts on that day.
pieces: In Jerusalem and Judah every pot will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, and all who offer sacrifices will come and use them to boil their meat. And on that day there will no longer be a trader in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.21: And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts; and all those sacrificing will come and take from them and boil [meat] in them. And there will no longer be a trader in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts in that day.

R.21: In Jerusalem and Judah every cooking pot will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. All the people who come to offer sacrifices will take some of these pots and cook the meat in them. At that time there will no longer be any traders in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: every pot in Jerusalem and Judah holy: the whole land made holy
decisions.reason: Not only the temple vessels but every household pot will be holy and fit for worship, so that all the worshipers who come can cook their sacrifices. The line between holy and common is not removed but pushed out to cover everything. Exodus 19:6 called Israel "a kingdom of priests and a holy nation".

decisions.choice: all who sacrifice will take and boil in them
decisions.reason: Worshipers cooked and ate the meat of their peace offerings at the sanctuary (Deuteronomy 12:17-18; 1 Samuel 2:13-14). So many will come that every pot in the land will be needed, and all of them are holy enough for that use.

decisions.choice: trader: or "Canaanite"
decisions.reason: The word is "Canaanite". The Canaanites, above all the Phoenicians of the coast, were known as traders, and the word came to mean "merchant" (Proverbs 31:24; Zephaniah 1:11; Job 40:30). Here it most likely means traders buying and selling in the temple. It may instead mean a Canaanite, one who is unclean and outside the covenant (compare Ezekiel 44:9). Either way, nothing unholy will be in the LORD's house.

decisions.choice: no more traders in the house of the LORD: compare John 2:16
decisions.reason: When Jesus drove the traders out of the temple courts, he said, "Do not make my Father's house a house of trade" (John 2:16). The words are not quoted from this verse, but they agree with it. The book ends here, with the LORD's house and all Jerusalem and Judah holy to him.

decisions.choice: [meat] (L); their meat (B); the meat (R); trader (every level)
decisions.reason: Every level says "trader", the most likely sense, and the footnote gives "Canaanite" (m3). The Hebrew says only "boil in them"; Literal brackets "meat", and Balanced and Readable say what is boiled.
